notes: Q2 2026 print (reported 2026-07-22, after close): total revenue $119.8B beat the prior ~$108B estimate handily; Cloud revenue $24.8B/+82% YoY and Cloud operating margin ~35.5% both individually exceed EVERY bull-case threshold this thesis had set (Cloud >=60%, margin >35%, backlog approaching $500B -- backlog actually hit $514B). Search grew +17% YoY, decelerating from Q1's +19% and landing in the BASE band (14-18%), not the bull band (>=22%) -- the base case's own stated bull-shift condition requires Cloud>60% AND Search>22% together, so by its own rule this does NOT yet trigger a full bull shift despite Cloud alone qualifying. The stock still dropped ~7-8% on the print (342.09 pre- to 319.74 post-) because full-year capex guidance was raised from $180-190B to $195-205B AND Alphabet posted its first-ever NEGATIVE quarterly FCF (-$5.9B) -- a live case of CLAUDE.md's cost-framing-panics-markets pattern, but a genuinely real (not purely optics) data point this time: TTM FCF is still ~$53B positive and cash/securities sit around $240B, so no liquidity concern, but the trend is the thing to watch. Pull-forward test: management described a 'supply-constrained environment' (demand exceeding capacity, not customers front-loading orders) and backlog GREW rather than shrank -- both point toward durable demand extension, not pull-forward, though the true test is whether Cloud revenue keeps converting backlog at pace AND FCF returns to positive over the next few quarters (the KPIs that would distinguish durable demand from pure cost overhang). Separately, the EU's top court rejected Google's final appeal on the Android antitrust case 2026-07-02, finalizing a EUR4.1B fine -- a real, concluded outcome, but a different and smaller matter than the still-pending US DOJ structural-remedies appeal (oral arguments expected late 2026/early 2027), which is unchanged this quarter. Multiple bands nudged down from the 22-25/28-31/32-36x framework set in May given real evidence the whole mega-cap AI-capex complex (MSFT, META, AMZN here) has been de-rating this same week on capex-fear -- named peer comps, not just GOOGL's own history.
